text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egypt's Mubarak sees basis for renewing PLO-Israel talks in Israel's Netanyahu's proposals; Egypt's envoy trying to get Palestinian leader Arafat to summit with Mubarak and Netanayhu.
- Ultra-Orthodox Jewish youth accused of burning Israeli flag says photographers didn't urge him to do it.
- Military intelligence estimate: As long as building continues on new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem there will not be peace negotiations.
- Finance Minister Meridor: Bank of Israel interest policy causing recession and unemployment.
- Globes survey: 45 percent disappointed in prime minister's performance; 14 percent surprised to the good.
- Netanyahu says there is no map outlining final settlement with Palestinians.
- U.S.: Netanyahu and Arafat must agree before summit.
- Israel notified by UEFA that it could be chosen to host final of European Cup or Cup Winners Cup in 2000.
- Former Jordanian air force commander wants defense ventures with Israel.
- Meridor forecasts 1997 inflation will be at high end of government target at 10 percent.
- Hanwha Ltd, Korea's 9th largest industrial concern, to send delegation to Israel next week.
- Palestinians say Netanyahu is conducting peace negotiations with himself.
- State will offer 10 percent of its share in Bezeq Telcom on Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on August 31.
